## Public collector

Sweeps the **whole job-title catalogue** into the shared `jobs` pool, whether or not anyone has asked for those roles yet. This is what makes a brand-new user’s dashboard non-empty the moment they finish onboarding.

Free sources only. **Apify is never involved here.**

**Sibling:** *Jobak — Collect (private · user terms)* runs this same pipeline against the titles real users actually chose — that is the one that matters to people who already signed up.

## 2 · The pointer

Calls the Postgres function **`collect_targets_public(p_batch)`** directly — no app round trip. Everything it needs is already in the database.

It takes the next **1** title, moves `collection_cursor` past it, and wraps at the end. The read and the advance happen under one row lock, so two overlapping runs can never take the same slice.

**The daily maths:** 1 title × 4 runs/hour × 24 h = **96 titles/day**, against a catalogue of ~95. One full sweep per day, by design.

Change the rate here and `p_batch` in the node body together, or the sweep stops fitting in a day.

## 1 · Config & lookups

**`Set Config` — edit before activating.** URLs and secrets live here, and the same values must appear in every Jobak workflow.

This workflow no longer calls the app at all: terms come from a Postgres function, and the lookups below are plain PostgREST reads.

⚠️ The three HTTP nodes here are set to **Execute Once**.

n8n runs a node once *per input item*. Without that flag, 247 region rows × 12 source rows produced **2,964** calls and timed the endpoint out.

## 3 · One term at a time

`Term Loop` hands the scraper a **single title per iteration**; `Scrape Free Sources` fans that title out across every free source — RemoteOK, Remotive, Arbeitnow, Jobicy, Himalayas, WeWorkRemotely, Wuzzuf.

**`maxAgeDays: 1`** in the request body keeps only what was posted today. Undated listings still pass — several feeds publish “latest N” without dating every row, and dropping those would empty whole sources.

`Unpack Scraper` attaches the target country and logs each source result, so a run that *lost* a source looks different from one where a source found nothing.

## 4 · Into the shared pool

`Prepare Job Rows` validates everything that reaches a typed column. This is a **bulk** insert — one bad timestamp or one unknown foreign key fails *every row in the batch*, not just its own. That is why `source_id` and `region_id` are resolved by name with a null fallback instead of being hardcoded.

`Insert Jobs (bulk)` upserts on `apply_url`, so the same posting found twice is one row.

`Log Run` writes `collection_runs` so an unattended run can be checked without opening n8n.

## Foreign-key lookups

Read once per run, then referenced downstream as `$('Fetch Regions')` and `$('Fetch Sources')`.

Ids are deliberately **not** hardcoded: a reseeded or reordered `sources` table used to break the bulk insert with a `23503` foreign-key violation.

An unknown code or key becomes `null` — an unattributed job still belongs in the pool.
